processing: A fine, straight strand green tea: fixed by heat, shaped into tight needles that keep their down, then dried without oxidation.
harvest_season: Spring, as is usual for downy famous greens; the youngest pickings are what give this style its silver tips.
appearance_dry: Tight, fine, straight strands covered in silvery down, glossy emerald underneath.
appearance_wet: Tender, lively green leaf that stays whole.
taste_profile: High, lasting aroma with a full, clean taste and a sweet return; the first steep is the most fragrant, the second the strongest, and the third and fourth keep a quiet perfume.

brewing.notes: General settings for a downy green. A glass shows off the needles; some down in the liquor is normal and no fault.

vintage_note: Sold like other Chinese famous greens: the current spring harvest, drunk within about a year. Ask for the picking date and look for abundant, clean down. Older stock simply fades.
description:
Shimen Yinfeng, 'Shimen silver peak', is a modern green tea from Shimen County in the north of Hunan. What marks it out is the leaf itself: fine, straight strands so covered in silver down that the green shows only underneath.

It is made as a shaped green tea, with the leaf fixed and then worked into tight, straight needles. Handling matters here, because keeping the down intact on a fine strand is what the style is judged by.

The usual description of it runs steep by steep: a clear fragrance in the first, more strength in the second, and a faint lasting perfume in the third and fourth. The cup is bright green, full and clean, with a sweet finish. Use cooler water and do not worry about the down clouding the liquor a little.

Buy it fresh, by picking date. Its prizes are provincial and national contest results, useful as background but no guide to the lot in front of you.
history: The tea was created in 1988. It was named a Hunan famous tea in 1993, took a second prize at the China Tea Cup in 1994, and in the same year won a gold award at the fifth Asia-Pacific international trade fair. In 2005 it was included among Hunan's ten famous teas.
